The product-spiked experiment also doesn't strongly discriminate among most mechanisms - all cluster around NLL ~-43, except M5 (clearly rejected). Product inhibition isn't manifesting strongly; perhaps the added product isn't high enough or the dominant mechanism doesn't involve product-catalyst interaction. M12 and M17 aren't favored, suggesting no strong product-induced deactivation. M13 is slightly preferred (2cat→inactive_cat2), hinting at catalyst dimerization-based deactivation.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
To discriminate catalyst dimerization/dimer-based mechanisms (M2, M3, M13) from monomeric deactivation (M9, M11, M14) and inhibitor-based (M10, M15), I should vary catalyst concentration dramatically. At high catalyst concentration:
- M2, M3, M13 predict non-linear rate scaling (dimerization of cat, rate ∝ [cat]² or lower effective [cat])
- M9, M11, M14, M20 predict linear scaling with catalyst (unimolecular deactivation)
- M19 (cat+catS→inactive) predicts 2nd order deactivation
- M7, M16, M18 involve S+catS or 2catS processes

Using HIGH catalyst (0.1 M) with moderate substrate (1.0 M) will magnify dimerization effects. Comparison with previous low-cat runs gives rate-order information on catalyst.
</hypothesis>
